transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I can’t stop thinking about the left side of my face. It looks crooked and messed up to me. I feel like people at the warehouse, or when I go salsa dancing, are noticing it all the time, even though they tell me they don’t see anything.
Do you think it’s possible that your face only seems crooked to you, even if other people really don’t see anything wrong?

I mean, people keep telling me they don’t notice anything, but I can’t see it that way. The left side looks crooked and messed up to me, and I feel like people at work or salsa night have to be noticing it.
Do you think there is any chance that your face is not actually crooked, even though it looks that way to you?

I guess there could be a chance, since people keep saying they don’t see it. But when I look at my face, the left side just looks crooked and messed up. I can’t stop thinking people at the warehouse or salsa night notice it.
Are you certain that the left side of your face is actually crooked?
I feel certain when I look at it. The left side just seems crooked and messed up to me, even though people keep telling me they don’t notice anything.
When you feel people are noticing you, is it mainly because you think they can see something wrong with the left side of your face?
Yeah, mostly. I feel like they’re looking at the left side of my face and seeing how crooked it looks. At the warehouse or salsa night, even if nobody says anything, I keep thinking they notice it.
If you were completely sure your face looked normal, would you still feel very anxious about people judging you in social situations?
I don’t think so—not nearly as much. It’s really the thought that the left side looks crooked and messed up that makes me feel like people are judging me, especially at work or salsa night.
Do you spend a lot of time checking the left side of your face in mirrors or other reflections?

Yeah. Before I go back out on the inventory floor, I’ll keep going into the bathroom to check the mirror. I fix my cap and rub at the same spot on my face. Sometimes I spend so long doing it that I’m late getting back, and my picking numbers fall behind. My boss has gotten on me about it again.
Are the mirror checking and rubbing something you do mainly because of worries about the left side of your face?

Yeah. I’m checking that side, trying to fix how it looks. I’ll mess with my cap and rub the same spot, then check again before going back out. Sometimes it takes so long my numbers fall behind and my boss gets on me.
Besides worries about how the left side of your face looks, do you get other unwanted thoughts that lead you to repeat behaviors or mental rituals?
I’m not sure what you mean by mental rituals. Mostly it’s the face thing—the checking and rubbing because I’m worried about that side.
Right now, do you believe the left side of your face is definitely deformed?
Yeah, I do. The left side looks crooked and messed up to me. People tell me they don’t see it, but I feel like everybody at the warehouse—or salsa night—is noticing it.
Do you ever avoid going to work or to salsa night because of how the left side of your face looks?

Yeah. I’ve skipped salsa nights and soccer, and even some family gatherings, because I don’t want people staring at me or taking pictures. I still go to work, but it’s been bad there too—I’ve been written up when I get delayed.
Other than your face, do you have any other upsetting thoughts that make you feel you have to do repeated rituals or checks?

It’s really just about my face. Before I go back onto the inventory floor, I keep going to the bathroom mirror, checking it, fixing my cap, rubbing that same spot. Sometimes I’m in there so long my picking numbers fall behind, and my boss gets on me again.
Has anyone ever told you that there really is even a slight crookedness or visible problem on the left side of your face?
No, not really. People keep telling me they don’t see anything wrong, but I still can’t stop seeing the left side as crooked and messed up.
Apart from worries about your face, do you usually feel afraid that people will judge or embarrass you in social situations?
No, not usually. It’s mainly when I’m thinking about my face—then I feel like people are looking at me or judging me.
